scholarships.title: Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship
scholarships.official_source: Chevening (UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office scheme), delivered by Cranfield University

eligibility: In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must be a citizen of and resident in one of the following countries at the point of application: Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, or Switzerland.
If you live in a European overseas territory, you may apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which you are a citizen.
Hold a postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field).
Have at least five years' relevant professional experience.

Be a mid-career professional with responsibilities for national or international security, and employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation.
Be working in a role with the potential to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness within their organisation and/or country.

Be able to demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to applying the knowledge and networks gained through the fellowship within their organisation and/or country on completion of the programme.

General Chevening Fellowship criteria: be a citizen of a fellowship-eligible country or territory; demonstrate the potential to rise to a position of leadership and influence; demonstrate the personal, intellectual, and interpersonal attributes reflecting this potential; return to your country of citizenship (country of award) for at least one year after your fellowship ends; and meet all programme-specific fellowship eligibility requirements.

General work-experience rule for Chevening Fellowships: a minimum of five years' work experience in a relevant related field, which equals 7,200 hours, calculated by multiplying weeks worked by hours per week (a working week comprises 35-60 hours and a working year comprises 40-50 weeks). 'If you do not already have the level of work experience required for your chosen fellowship programme, you will be unable to submit your application.'
You do not need to meet the work experience requirement in one period of employment; applicants can submit up to fifteen different employment periods.
existing.eligibility_summary: Must meet the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria plus the programme-specific rules: citizenship and residence in one of 35 listed European countries, a postgraduate qualification, at least five years' relevant professional experience, and a security-related role with influence potential.
benefits: Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship, including pre-arranged accommodation (the page states 'close to Oxford')
A monthly personal living allowance (stipend), confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Arrival allowance, paid on arrival in the UK
Departure allowance, where applicable to the fellowship type
A travel top-up allowance to attend events in London, for those in receipt of non-London stipends
A contribution of up to £75 for TB testing where this is required for the visa application
Reimbursement of the UK visa application fee for the fellow only
Reimbursement of the Immigration Health Surcharge, or a contribution towards travel insurance of up to £200

A research allowance as a contribution towards the cost of producing a thesis/dissertation where required for the course, or for conducting research associated with the programme, confirmed in the Final Award Letter

requirements: Meet the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria and all programme-specific requirements.
Apply through the Chevening online application system reached from the relevant European country/territory page.
Demonstrate five years' (7,200 hours) of relevant professional experience, calculated automatically from the weeks and hours you enter.

Ensure the employing organisation will release you for the six-week programme: 'it is your responsibility to ensure that they will release you if you are selected for a Chevening Fellowship. The British embassy/high commission or the Chevening Secretariat cannot intervene in this.'
Secure and comply with the UK entry clearance (visa) requirements applicable to the fellowship, including medical clearance.
On return of the acceptance form, agree to abide by the Chevening Fellowship terms and conditions for the duration of the award.
documents: The completed Chevening Fellowship application form submitted through the online application system
Return of the award acceptance form after selection (terms and conditions are accepted on return of this form)

Medical clearance for the UK entry clearance (visa) - the terms and conditions state the award is contingent on the Fellow's 'ability to procure relevant UK entry clearance (a visa) and receive medical clearance'

Your Final Award Letter (FAL), which confirms all financial elements of the award, the stipend amount, tenure dates, and whether accommodation, a research allowance, arrival and departure allowances apply
Any compulsory documentation requested by the Secretariat during the award - failure to return it can lead to stipend suspension
application_method: Confirm you are a citizen and resident of one of the 35 listed European countries and that you meet the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria.
Check your five-year (7,200 hour) work experience total using the published calculation method before submitting.
Apply through the Chevening online application system reached from the 'apply today' link for your country/territory.
Answer the eligibility questions and complete each section of the application form, including your employment history and research interests.
Attend any selection or interview stage notified by Chevening or your local Chevening team.
On offer, return the acceptance form to accept the terms and conditions.
Attend the pre-departure briefing hosted by the British embassy or high commission in your home country before travelling.
Attend the welcome reception and/or induction with the Chevening Secretariat on arrival in the UK.
Complete and return all report requests and surveys during the award, and attend the feedback session at the end.
existing.selection_notes: Chevening publishes the four general Fellowship objectives - supporting mid-career professionals in positions of leadership and influence, offering dynamic training/professional development/research relevant to professional interests and UK international strategic priorities, increasing the breadth and diversity of Chevening awards, and supporting FCDO foreign policy priorities by creating lasting relationships with future leaders, influencers and decision-makers. For this programme the assessment is against the general Chevening Fellowship criteria plus the published programme-specific requirements, and against the needs of a cohort drawn from the listed European countries. Chevening Fellowships are 'an important element of Britain's public diplomacy effort', and fellows are active in their field or subject. Chevening does not publish a separate scoring framework or interview format for this programme; applications for Chevening Scholarships follow the published sifting, reading committee, embassy shortlist and interview stages, while Chevening states that 'Application timelines for Chevening Fellowships vary.'
existing.best_fit: Mid-career professionals who are citizens AND residents of one of the 35 listed European countries, hold a postgraduate qualification or equivalent professional training, have at least five years' relevant professional experience (7,200 hours) in defence, security, government, diplomacy, policing, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, academia, media, energy/infrastructure or international organisations, and can show leadership potential and a commitment to applying what they learn on return.
existing.notes: Deferral: 'Applications to defer awards will only be granted in the case of pregnancy.' Extensions: 'Extensions to the original fellowship duration may be permitted in exceptional circumstances, but the total duration must not exceed 12 months. All extensions are subject to the availability of funds and assessed on a case-by-case basis. Extensions are not automatic and should not be assumed.' Return home: 'You are expected to return to your home country for at least one year on completion of your fellowship.' Dependants: 'All Chevening Awards are calculated to support fellow costs only. There are no financial or welfare provisions for dependants of Chevening Fellows. It is strongly advised that Fellows do not bring dependants to the UK', and 'The Chevening Programme will not endorse the visa applications of, nor provide travel for, dependants.' Other conditions: no transfer to any course other than that confirmed in the Final Award Letter; no other publicly funded award during the fellowship period; approval required before any part-time employment or internship outside the approved programme; cannot serve as an official government representative during the fellowship; must not be outside the UK for more than 30 days in total (pro-rata: 3-month tenure up to 7 days outside the UK), and absences without prior notice may suspend the stipend or end the award; must cite Chevening Fellowships in publications; breach may result in withdrawal of the award. Stipend suspension may occur if fellowship terms and conditions are not complied with, if compulsory documentation is not returned, or if the Fellow elects to return home early and submit work from overseas.
existing.duration: Six weeks, in two cohorts: Cohort 1 25 January - 5 March 2027; Cohort 2 15 March - 23 April 2027
existing.application_period: Applications are open and close at 11:00 (UTC) on 12 October 2026. The programme itself runs in two cohorts in 2027: 25 January - 5 March 2027 and 15 March - 23 April 2027.
